_comment: The licences this project accepts in its PRODUCTION dependency tree, enforced
The tree is the `npm ls --omit=dev --all --workspaces` closure, so it is what a
self-hoster actually installs and ships; devDependencies are out of scope by
design, because none of them reaches a user's machine.
`allow` is a POLICY list, not a snapshot of what happens to be installed: a new
MIT dependency should not fail the gate, while a new licence nobody has ruled on
must. `deny` is checked FIRST and independently, so a copyleft licence is a hard
failure even if someone also adds it to `allow` — H-Vault is MIT and is
redistributed as source and as container images, and a reciprocal obligation
reaching that tree is a licensing defect, not a preference.
`firstParty` names this repository's own workspace packages. They are
`private: true`, so npm reports them UNLICENSED regardless of the `license`
field in their package.json; they are never published, and their declared
There is no per-package exception list. If one is ever genuinely needed it
belongs in .testfortress/suppressions.json with an owner, a reason and an
expiry — not here, where it would be permanent and unreviewed.
